annotation.title_clean: Directive (EU) 2024/2853 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2024 on liability for defective products and repealing Council Directive 85/374/EEC
annotation.title_en: Directive (EU) 2024/2853 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2024 on liability for defective products and repealing Council Directive 85/374/EEC
annotation.authors_or_issuer: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union
annotation.summary_en: The revised EU Product Liability Directive replaces Directive 85/374/EEC. It extends strict no-fault liability to software, AI systems, digital manufacturing files and related services, covers learning-capable products and cybersecurity defects, and eases claimants' burden of proof through disclosure duties and rebuttable presumptions. Member States must transpose it by 9 December 2026.
key_provisions_or_claims: Software, including AI systems, is a product, and AI providers are treated as manufacturers.
Defectiveness takes into account continued learning, interconnection effects, cybersecurity and safety requirements.
Courts can order evidence disclosure and presume defectiveness or causation in technically complex cases.
Manufacturers stay liable for defects from software updates, related services or missing security updates within their control.
Applies to products placed on the market after 9 December 2026; 10-year expiry, 25 years for latent injury.
